summary: This informational memo covers security for provider-provisioned VPNs. It describes threats, including those from malicious behaviour inside or outside the network, and defensive techniques, and lists security requirements for such services.

eli5.summary: A private network run by someone else needs protection from bad guys. This document lists the dangers and the defences.

subtitle: A checklist of threats, defenses and requirements for VPNs that a service provider builds and runs for its customers.

tldr.problem: Customers of provider-provisioned VPNs (PPVPNs) share a provider's core network with other customers, so they need to know what can go wrong and what protection to expect.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC defines a trusted-zone reference model, lists data plane and control plane threats, reviews defenses such as encryption, authentication, filtering and isolation, states user and provider security requirements, and ends with a template for evaluating any specific PPVPN technology.
tldr.outcome: It is a framework and a checklist, not a protocol. It deliberately does not say which mechanisms every technology must implement, and it does not analyze any particular technology.

facts.label: Trusted zones
facts.value: Each PPVPN, plus the PPVPN core

today: RFC 4111 is Informational and is updated by RFC 8996. It is a framework and checklist, not a protocol, and nothing in the text marks it as replaced.

sections.title: Purpose and Scope
sections.content:
Security is an integral part of Provider-Provisioned Virtual Private Network (PPVPN) services, a VPN that is configured and managed by the service provider rather than by the customer. The motivation for provider-provisioned layer 2 and layer 3 VPNs is given in RFC 4110 and RFC 4031, and this document supplies the security side.

It first describes threats and defensive techniques, covering problems caused by malicious behavior and by negligent or incorrect behavior of the providers. It then discusses user and provider security requirements, and finally defines a template for describing the security characteristics of a specific PPVPN technology.

The RFC is explicit about its limits. It does not analyze specific technologies, it does not formulate precise requirements on each technology, and special considerations from IP mobility within PPVPNs are out of scope.
sections.eli5: Imagine a company that builds a private tunnel network for you inside its big shared one. This document asks: how could someone mess with it, and how do we stop them?

sections.title: The Trusted-Zone Reference Model
sections.content:
The RFC uses a few device names. A CE (Customer Edge) device sits in the customer network and faces the provider. A PE (Provider Edge) device is the provider equipment that faces the customer. A P router is in the provider core with no interfaces toward customers, and it does not have to maintain VPN state.

The model treats each PPVPN as a trusted zone and the PPVPN core as another trusted zone. The main concern is breaches from the outside of a zone to the inside. Even when several providers share one core, it appears to users as a single zone of trust. Where the core also offers Internet access, a transit point joins the zones.

The key requirement of a VPN is that the security of its trusted zone is not compromised by sharing the core infrastructure with other VPNs. Attacks that start inside the same zone as their target, and security issues that are independent of whether a network is a PPVPN, are out of scope.
sections.eli5: Think of each customer's network as a fenced yard, and the provider's core as the street between the yards. The rule is that sharing the street must never let someone climb into your yard.

sections.title: Security Threats
sections.content:
A successful attack may cause observation, modification or deletion of user data, replay of data, injection of non-authentic data, traffic pattern analysis, disruption of connectivity, or degraded service quality. The threats may come from users of other PPVPNs on the same provider, the provider or its staff, people with physical access to a provider site, people using social engineering on provider staff, or attackers on the Internet at large. Attacks become easier and more likely as the shared infrastructure grows from one provider to cooperating providers to the global Internet.

Data plane attacks are on the customer's traffic: unauthorized observation (sniffing), modification, insertion of non-authentic traffic through spoofing and replay, deletion, traffic pattern analysis, and denial of service. The RFC notes that most PPVPN users consider traffic pattern analysis significantly less of a concern than the others.

Control plane attacks are on the structures the provider runs:

  • denial of service on infrastructure, including one customer's activity starving others;
  • attacks via management interfaces, and social engineering of provider staff;
  • cross-connection of traffic between PPVPNs, such as a site connected into the wrong VPN or two VPNs merged;
  • attacks on PPVPN routing protocols, on route separation, and on address space separation;
  • attacks on other control traffic such as LDP, RSVP-TE, IKE, L2TP, BGP-based and RADIUS-based membership discovery.

The RFC says anecdotal evidence suggests cross-connection is one of the largest security concerns of PPVPN users or would-be users.
sections.eli5: Bad things can happen to the messages themselves, like peeking, changing or copying them, and to the machines that steer the messages, like being tricked into sending your mail to the wrong yard.

sections.title: Defensive Techniques and Monitoring
sections.content:
The defenses are described as methods, not requirements for every implementation. The RFC reminds readers that nothing is ever 100% secure, and that it is often enough to make an attack cost more than the adversary would spend.

  • Encryption. It can be applied on the CE-PE link, between PEs, or CE to CE, depending on which part of the path is trusted. IPsec is named as the security protocol of choice at the IP layer. Encryption adds processing load, configuration complexity and packet length, and it hides content from filters and from differentiated services. Management traffic can be protected with SSH, SNMP v3, TLS or IPsec.
  • Authentication. It covers VPN membership, management systems, peer control protocols such as LDP and BGP, and remote access users, for example via RADIUS or DIAMETER.
  • Access control. Filters act on one direction of traffic, while firewalls see both sides of a conversation and can keep more state. Management interfaces can be reachable only out of band.
  • Isolation and aggregation. Separate infrastructure helps, but sharing is the point of VPNs, so limits such as rate limiting, per-VPN queues and reserved control-plane resources protect well-behaved users from others.
  • Process. Providers need operational processes against misconfiguration, and services that can be tested for correct connectivity.

Section 6 adds that PPVPN services should also detect and report attacks, successful or not, with a monitoring channel that is itself secured and does not flood the network (for example, several events can be reported in one message).
sections.eli5: To keep the yards safe you can lock the messages in boxes, check everyone's ID, put guards at the gates, and make sure nobody uses up the whole street. You also want an alarm that tells you when someone tries the gate.

sections.title: User and Provider Security Requirements
sections.content:
Section 7 lists what users may expect. It does not say a PPVPN must satisfy all of them to be secure.

  • Isolation: address separation (a VPN can use the full Internet address range, including private ranges, without interfering with other VPNs), routing separation, and traffic separation.
  • Protection against intrusion, denial of service and spoofing, at the same level as a private network.
  • Confidentiality, integrity, anti-replay and CE authentication, which means an outsider cannot install a CE and pretend to belong to a VPN.

The RFC adds that even private networks do not always meet confidentiality, integrity and anti-replay, so these apply only if the comparable private service also offered them.

Section 8 turns these into provider requirements for the core and the access link. Examples include authenticating control plane sessions (IGP, BGP and LDP sessions may use TCP MD5 or IPsec), hiding provider infrastructure routers from outside users, rate limiting on user interfaces, limiting the number of prefixes a customer may advertise to a PE, and per-class access QoS checks. Hardware or software bugs that cause breaches are out of scope.
sections.eli5: Customers want their own yard to stay separate, stay safe from break-ins, and keep their messages secret and unchanged. The provider has to build the street so all of that can be true.

sections.title: The Security Evaluation Template
sections.content:
Section 9 gives authors of PPVPN approaches a template, and says an evaluation using it should appear in each approach's applicability statement. It starts with assertions such as complete IP address space separation for each L3 VPN, a means to prevent and to detect improper cross-connection of sites, and confidentiality, sender authentication, integrity and replay protection for user data on the CE-PE link, in a single- or multi-provider backbone, or in the Internet used as backbone.

For each assertion, an approach is rated, for example as not applicable, completely or partially addressed by the base approach or by an optional extension, addressed beyond the scope of the approach, or not met. The template ends with free-form questions on PPVPN-specific denial of service, on unstable or malicious customer networks, and on any approach-specific vulnerabilities.

The Security Considerations section notes that some threats have already been observed in running networks, such as DoS and intrusion attacks from the Internet against provider infrastructure, and CE equipment overwhelming PE equipment with traffic or routing information. Operational and provisioning errors are cited by providers as a prime concern.
sections.eli5: The template is a report card. For every promise of safety, the people who design a VPN have to say whether they fully, partly or do not keep it.
